2609.10923.title: Structurally Speaking: Motif-Oriented Graph Captioning through Bidirectional Graph-Text Translation
2609.10923.paper_summary: Graph captions should help readers understand graph structure, rather than simply translate adjacency matrices into long textual edge lists. A useful graph caption abstracts connectivity into recognizable motifs, such as hubs, paths, cycles, cliques, and bridges, because these motifs provide compact structural units that are easier to read, compare, and recover. In this paper, we study motif-oriented graph captioning as a bidirectional graph-text translation task, where captions must both preserve enough topology for graph recovery and express the graph through concise motif-level descriptions. We show that direct prompting of GPT-5.1 often produces graph-recoverable captions by enumerating node-to-node connections, but these captions are verbose and can contain inconsistent motif interpretations. To address this gap, we introduce Structurally Speaking, a lightweight structured prompting protocol that guides translation between explicit connectivity and motif-level abstraction. Experiments on a synthetic motif-based dataset show that structured prompting produces shorter and more motif-consistent captions while maintaining comparable graph recovery. These results suggest that explicit topology-to-motif reasoning guidance can make LLM-generated graph captions more interpretable without model fine-tuning.
2609.10923.paper_summary_zh: 圖表標題應該幫助讀者理解圖表結構，而不僅僅是將鄰接矩陣翻譯成冗長的文本邊列表。<lb/>有用的圖表標題將連接性抽象為可識別的主題，例如樞紐、路徑、循環、團體和橋樑，因為這些主題提供了更易於閱讀、比較和恢復的緊湊結構單元。<lb/>在本文中，我們將以主題為導向的圖表標題研究作為一種雙向圖-文本翻譯任務，其中標題必須同時保留足夠的拓撲以便於圖的恢復，並通過簡潔的主題級描述來表達圖。<lb/>我們顯示，直接提示GPT-5.1通常通過列舉節點之間的連接來產生可恢復的圖表標題，但這些標題冗長且可能包含不一致的主題解釋。<lb/>為了解決這一問題，我們引入了Structurally Speaking，一種輕量級的結構化提示協議，指導在明確的連接性和主題級抽象之間的翻譯。<lb/>在一個合成的基於主題的數據集上的實驗顯示，結構化提示產生了更短且更一致的主題標題，同時保持了可比的圖恢復能力。<lb/>這些結果表明，明確的拓撲到主題的推理指導可以使LLM生成的圖表標題更具可解釋性，而無需對模型進行微調。
